chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Breast-feeding does not make (marriage) prohibited except that which causes the flesh to grow and the bones to strengthen.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of breast-feeding required to make marriage prohibited between two people in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for establishing permanent kinship (mahramiyyah) through breast-feeding, asserting that mere sucking is insufficient. It emphasizes that the intake must be substantial enough to nourish the infant's body, thereby building flesh and strengthening bones, a criterion widely accepted in Shia fiqh to distinguish between temporary and permanent nursing relationships.
